project: DixScript Rust Port — Value Resolution Phase 2
description: Plan for porting FunctionInterpreter.cs and ValueResolver.cs. Core logic is preserved; the port improves ownership semantics, eliminates mutable-field swapping via explicit parameter threading, uses typed Result errors throughout, and removes dead/duplicate code identified in C#.

shared_decisions.debug_logging: Same pattern as Phase 1: DebugConfig cached at construction. Every log site is guarded by `if self.debug_config.is_enabled { … }`. format!() never executes when debug is off.
shared_decisions.position_handling: All errors carry a Position directly from the AST node. No redundant line/column fields anywhere.
shared_decisions.data_context_sharing: ValueResolver and FunctionInterpreter share the data context via Rc<RefCell<HashMap<String, DixValue>>>. Rust equivalent of C#'s pass-by-reference dictionary. Both hold a clone of the same Rc. Access is sequential (never truly concurrent) so runtime borrow panics are not a risk.
shared_decisions.symbol_table_borrowing: Both resolver and interpreter borrow &SymbolTable with lifetime 'a. Resolver owns the interpreter, so the lifetime naturally flows through.
shared_decisions.quick_functions_cloned_once: The AST's QuickFunctions slice is cloned into the interpreter at construction time. This decouples the interpreter from the AST borrow, letting the resolver mutate ast.data freely while the interpreter holds its own copy of the function definitions. Cold-path cost — acceptable.
shared_decisions.error_strategy: Replace throw/catch chains with Result<DixValue, InterpreterError> (interpreter) and Result<ValueResolutionResult, ResolverError> (resolver). Every variant carries Position. The C# pattern of catching broad Exception and re-wrapping as FunctionExecutionException becomes a single top-level ? operator per call site.

function_interpreter.summary: Executes QuickFunction bodies at compile time. Evaluates expressions, binds parameters, dispatches statements, resolves identifiers with 4-tier priority, handles imported functions, lambdas, and recursive calls.

struct_layout.name: FunctionInterpreter<'a>
struct_layout.rationale: Lifetime 'a ties the interpreter to the borrowed SymbolTable. All other state is owned.

execution_model.title: Parameter Threading — eliminates mutable-field swapping
execution_model.problem_in_csharp: C# swaps currentContext, currentCallScopeContext, and currentExecutingNamespace as mutable fields on self before each nested Execute call, then restores them in a finally block. In Rust this pattern fights the borrow checker — &mut self is held across recursive calls that also need &mut self.
execution_model.rust_solution: Thread execution state as explicit parameters down the call chain. Every method that needs them receives: (1) context: &mut ExecutionContext, (2) scope_context: &HashMap<String, String>, (3) namespace: Option<&ImportedNamespace>. No save/restore. No interior mutability on these fields. The call stack itself becomes the 'stack' of nested contexts.
execution_model.signature_example: fn execute(&mut self, function: &QuickFunction, arguments: &[Expression], context: &mut ExecutionContext, scope_context: &HashMap<String, String>, namespace: Option<&ImportedNamespace>) -> Result<DixValue, InterpreterError>
execution_model.cascade: execute → execute_statement → evaluate_expression — all carry the same three parameters. This is more verbose than C# but explicit, borrow-safe, and zero runtime overhead.

error_type.name: InterpreterError
error_type.note: Every variant carries Position. Display impl formats a human-readable message per variant. Implements std::error::Error. No generic 'message' catch-all — every failure path has a specific variant.

methods.note: Receives already-cloned quick_functions. Caches DebugConfig. Initializes recursion_depth=0, empty lambda_registry, empty log_statements.
Borrows data_context via borrow_mut(), inserts key/value. Debug log gated.

Public entry. Increments recursion_depth (checked against limit first). Calls bind_parameters, then loops through function.body statements. Explicit return on Return statement. Implicit return = last statement result. Decrements recursion_depth on all exit paths (Rust: natural drop, no finally needed — depth is decremented before the Result is returned).

Evaluates arguments or default values. Defines each param in context. Returns Err on count mismatch or eval failure. Default values: only missing args past the required count get defaults — matches C# logic exactly.

4-tier priority: (1) execution context, (2) scope context → data context lookup, (3) path-suffix search in data context, (4) direct key lookup in data context. Returns InterpreterError::UndefinedVariable with scope debug info on miss.

Evaluates condition. Executes then-branch or else-branch. Early return on Return statement inside branch. Returns Null if no branch taken.

Operators: - (negate), ! / not, ++, --, ~? (bitwise NOT). Type checks for numeric ops.

Handles Array (bounds check → IndexOutOfBounds), Object (key lookup), String (char at index).

Looks up key in symbol_table.configs. Returns ConfigKeyNotFound on miss.

Lambda → store placeholder string AND register in lambda_registry. Prefixed constructors route to their handlers. EnumValue → evaluate_enum_access.

Combined into one method: returns the accumulated logs and leaves the vec empty. Matches the pattern resolver uses (get then clear). Uses std::mem::take for zero-copy drain.

improvements_over_csharp: No mutable field swapping. currentContext, currentCallScopeContext, and currentExecutingNamespace are threaded as parameters. Eliminates the save/restore/finally pattern entirely.
DebugConfig cached at construction. format!() never called when debug is off.
All errors are typed variants of InterpreterError. Every variant carries Position. No string-formatting at the error throw site.
GetLogStatements + ClearLogStatements merged into drain_log_statements using mem::take.
Lambda placeholder string improved: the lambda_registry stores a typed (Vec<String>, Expression) tuple instead of relying on the interpreter to find the Lambda in the original AST.
recursion_depth is decremented naturally before the Result is returned — no finally block needed.

value_resolver.summary: Orchestrates the full compile-time resolution pass. Resolves enums → builds data context → discovers function calls → iteratively executes them → replaces calls in AST with computed values → resolves remaining identifier references.

struct_layout.name: ValueResolver<'a>
struct_layout.rationale: Lifetime 'a for the borrowed SymbolTable. Owns the AST and mutates it in place.

fields.name: ast
fields.note: Owned. Mutated during resolution (enum replacement, function call replacement, identifier resolution). Returned in the result.

fields.name: symbol_table
fields.note: Read-only. Used for enum lookups, namespace resolution, scope validation.

fields.name: interpreter
fields.note: Owned. Created once with cloned quick_functions. Persists across all ExecuteFunctionCall invocations (lambda_registry accumulates).

fields.name: data_context
fields.note: Shared Rc with interpreter. Resolver writes after function execution; interpreter reads during.

fields.name: resolved_values
fields.note: Records every successfully resolved location → value. Used for the dump and final statistics.

fields.name: log_statements
fields.note: Accumulated from interpreter after each call (drained via drain_log_statements).

fields.name: resolution_history
fields.note: Ordered log of every resolution attempt (success or failure). Populated lazily — argument strings are only formatted when the dump is generated.

fields.name: start_time
fields.note: std::time::Instant for wall-clock duration. Rust equivalent of C# DateTime.Now subtraction.

ownership_model.ast_mutation_strategy: The resolver owns the AST. Enum replacement and function-call replacement rebuild affected DataEntry nodes and swap them into the entries vec. The ast.data field is a mutable owned DataSection. Replacement is done by index lookup (FindEntryIndexByPath equivalent) followed by direct index assignment on the entries vec — no ImmutableArray reconstruction per replacement.
ownership_model.ast_mutation_improvement: C# rebuilds the entire DataSection ImmutableArray on every single replacement via entries.ToArray() + ToImmutableArray(). In Rust, ast.data.entries is a Vec<DataEntry>. Individual entry replacement is O(1) index assignment. The entries vec is only reallocated if its capacity is exceeded (which it won't be — no entries are added, only replaced).
ownership_model.interpreter_lifetime: Interpreter borrows symbol_table with the same 'a as the resolver. quick_functions are owned by the interpreter (cloned once). data_context is Rc — both sides hold a clone.
ownership_model.data_context_access_pattern: Sequential, never concurrent. Resolver calls interpreter.execute() which reads data_context. execute() returns. Resolver then writes to data_context. borrow()/borrow_mut() are always paired within a single statement or short block.

resolution_phases.name: Enum Pre-Resolution
resolution_phases.description: Walk all DATA entries. Replace every EnumValue and EnumAccess expression with its integer value. Both local and imported enums. Must complete before function resolution so enums are available as integers in data_context.
resolution_phases.improvement: Collect all replacements in a single pass, then apply them. Avoids repeated partial AST reconstructions.

resolution_phases.name: Initial Data Context Build
resolution_phases.description: Populate data_context with all literal values from DATA. Flat properties, table properties, group array items, object properties. Nested objects are flattened with full paths. IdentifierValue references are resolved if their target is already in context.
resolution_phases.improvement: Use PathBuilder consistently. The C# code mixes manual string concatenation with PathBuilder calls — Rust version routes all path construction through PathBuilder.

resolution_phases.name: Function Call Discovery
resolution_phases.description: Delegates to ASTWalker (already ported in Phase 1). Returns Vec<FunctionCallInfo>.
resolution_phases.note: No changes needed — just calls the Phase 1 walker.

resolution_phases.name: Iterative Resolution Loop
resolution_phases.description: Iterate over unresolved calls. Execute each. On success: replace in AST + update data_context. On UndefinedVariable: defer (dependencies not yet resolved). On other error: record failure and remove from unresolved set. Repeat until all resolved, all stuck, or max iterations reached.
resolution_phases.improvement: Use a Vec<FunctionCallInfo> + index-based swap-remove for the unresolved set instead of HashSet iteration. Better cache locality on the hot loop. Deferred calls stay in the vec; resolved/failed are swapped out.

resolution_phases.name: Remaining Identifier Resolution
resolution_phases.description: After all functions are resolved, walk DATA again looking for IdentifierValue nodes whose targets are now in data_context. Replace them with the resolved values.
resolution_phases.note: Only runs if all function calls resolved successfully.

error_type.name: ResolverError
error_type.note: ExecutionFailed wraps InterpreterError for function execution failures — preserves the inner error chain.

methods.note: Takes ownership of ast. Borrows symbol_table. Creates shared data_context Rc. Clones ast.quick_functions into interpreter. Caches DebugConfig. Initializes BuiltinCallResolver.

Main orchestrator. Runs phases 1-5 in order. Returns ValueResolutionResult with owned AST, metrics, errors, logs, and history. On any fatal error, returns a failed result with the AST in its current state.
Walks all entries, collects replacements, applies them. Logs counts of local vs imported enum resolutions.

Recursive. Handles: EnumValue (local and imported via dotted name), ExpressionValue containing EnumAccess, Array (recurse items), ObjectLiteral (recurse properties), PrefixedConstructor (recurse args). Returns (new_value, local_count, imported_count) tuple.
Populates data_context. SimpleProperty, TableProperty, GroupArray, ObjectProperty all handled. IdentifierValue resolution attempted (best-effort at this stage).

Recursive check: returns false for QuickFuncCall, IdentifierValue, InterpolatedString, ExpressionValue. Returns true for all terminal types. Arrays/Objects/PrefixedConstructors recurse into their children.
Converts literal AST values to DixValue. All numeric types, strings, booleans, dates, null, hex colors, arrays, objects, tuples, blobs, regex.

Routes to execute_imported_function_call if namespace is set. Otherwise: validate scope, find function in quick_functions, create ExecutionContext, call interpreter.execute(), drain logs, update data_context with result.
methods.improvement: Scope validation returns a typed ResolverError::InvalidFunctionScope with the allowed scopes included.

methods.note: Resolves namespace, finds function, creates context, calls interpreter.execute() with namespace parameter. Updates data_context.

Finds the entry by path. Navigates into the entry's value tree to find the exact call site (may be nested in objects, arrays, tuples). Replaces with the computed AST value. Updates the entry in place via index assignment.
methods.improvement: Entry replacement is a direct vec index write — no ImmutableArray rebuild.

methods.note: Recursive dispatcher. Checks if the current value's path matches the target location. If direct match: replace. If parent path: recurse into ObjectLiteral, Array, or PrefixedConstructor.
methods.return_type: (Value, bool) — new value and whether replacement occurred.

methods.note: Checks if a Value is a QuickFuncCall or ExpressionValue wrapping one (or ImportedFunctionCall) matching the target callInfo. Returns (should_replace, replacement_value).
Walks DATA entries looking for IdentifierValue nodes. If their target is now in data_context, replaces them with the resolved AST value.
Checks function's allowed scopes against the call's scope path. Global scope functions always pass. Descendant matching via scope_is_descendant.
Checks if callPath is a descendant of allowedPath. Skips array-index segments (e.g. [0]) during comparison.
Converts a computed DixValue back to an AST Value node for insertion into the tree. Handles all DixTypes. Arrays, objects, and tuples recurse.

Formats a human-readable dump of the entire resolution pass. Summary stats, per-function usage, successful resolutions with arguments and results, failures with error messages, final resolved values grouped by type, captured log statements.
Short human-readable representation for dump output. Truncates long strings/arrays.

improvements_over_csharp: AST entry replacement via direct Vec index assignment — eliminates repeated ToArray() + ToImmutableArray() per replacement. Single O(1) write per call site.
DebugConfig cached at construction. All diagnostic logs gated.
Iterative resolution loop uses Vec + swap_remove instead of HashSet iteration. Better cache locality.
PathBuilder used consistently for all path construction. No mixed manual concatenation.
ResolutionRecord argument strings are formatted lazily — only when generate_resolution_dump is actually called. Saves allocation on the hot resolution loop.
std::time::Instant used instead of DateTime.Now for duration measurement. More precise, no system clock overhead.
Error types are typed variants (ResolverError) not string messages. ExecutionFailed wraps InterpreterError to preserve the inner error chain.

dead_code_removed.reason: Not called by any active replacement path. ReplaceInValueStructure + CheckAndReplaceValue handle all replacement logic via path matching. This method uses a different (and less reliable) name-based matching approach.
Not called anywhere in the resolver. CheckAndReplaceValue covers the same check with more thorough matching (handles ExpressionValue wrapping and ImportedFunctionCall).
Only used in an error log inside ReplaceFunctionCall when entry lookup fails. Folded into the error variant's data — the entry paths are available from the entries vec directly.

stub_removal: Remove the commented-out stub lines for value_resolver and function_interpreter — they are now real modules.

implementation_order.reason: ValueResolver depends on FunctionInterpreter. Port the interpreter first so the resolver can reference it.
Depends on FunctionInterpreter, ASTWalker (Phase 1), and all supporting types.
